text.p: Creditanstalt chief executive Guido Schmidt-Chiari resigned immediately after Bank Austria received the go ahead from the European Commission to take over Creditanstalt, the banker said in a magazine interview.

"I handed over a letter to the president of the supervisory board in which I declared my resignation effective after the end of the ordinary general meeting," Schmidt-Chiari told current affairs magazine Profil, which goes on sale on Monday.
The European Commission gave the green light to the 17.2 billion schillings ($1.4 billion) merger of Austria's first and second banks on March 11.
Schmidt-Chiari, chief executive of Creditanstalt since 1988 and who mounted a spirited campaign to stop the hostile bid, said the price Bank Austria paid for its rival was "certainly not too low".
The banker, who said he would remain active but would not work in the banking sector, also gave his blessing to the new Austrian megabank, saying it definitely had good prospects in the long term.

On Friday, Creditanstalt board member Max Kothbauer said he had offered his resignation to CA's supervisory board and to Gerhard Randa (chief executive of Bank Austria) and assumed that all other board members had also resigned.
